alert.title: Warm but wrong seat:
alert.text: Guido asked for email, and Jenny's Oct 21 email was **opened 3 times with 6 link clicks** — but he runs **drug substance (chemistry/CMC)**, not biology. Use him as a door to Angelini's **disease biology / translational** team.

items: **Guido was just in Korea** (business trip to meet partners, ~1 week ago) — the most natural opener for a Seoul-based CEO.
**No direct overlap found** between Amos and Guido (schools, employers, co-authors or events) in public sources.

**Korean biotech ties at Angelini:** Angelini sells **cenobamate** in Europe under a license from Korea's **SK Biopharmaceuticals**, and in Oct 2024 signed an option deal (up to $360M) on **CV-01** from Korea's **Cureverse**. Angelini already trusts Korean science partners.
**Angelini Ventures** (€300M fund) is expanding into **Asian biotech** with a new Singapore office — a possible second door for Meteor.

lead_with.title: Be honest about fit
lead_with.text: Say it plainly: SLACS serves biology and biomarker teams, not drug-substance chemistry. Ask Guido **who in Angelini's disease biology / translational team** should see it. Scientists respect a straight ask.

lead_with.title: Rare disease is new for them
lead_with.text: Catalyst brings **Firdapse (LEMS)**, **Agamree (Duchenne)** and **Fycompa (epilepsy)**. Rare neuromuscular and epilepsy tissue is small and precious — exactly where **location-precise cell isolation** helps.

lead_with.title: Korea-friendly partner
lead_with.text: Angelini already licenses from SK Biopharmaceuticals and Cureverse. A Seoul-born platform company is not a stranger to them.

person.name: Guido Furlotti
person.text: **28 years at Angelini.** Drug Substance Development Science Lead since Jan 2026. Before that: Fine Chemicals Business Project Manager (2022–2026, Aprilia — process development, tech transfer, CMC, and evaluating **CDMO requests for proposal** for business development) and Process Development Manager (2020–2022, ran five lab units: flow chemistry, kilo-lab, synthesis, purification, control). Business training at **LUISS Business School**. A chemistry/CMC and partnering person, not a tissue biologist.

company.text: Angelini Pharma is the pharmaceutical arm of Angelini Industries, a family-owned Italian group founded in Ancona in 1919 and based in Rome. CEO: **Sergio Marullo di Condojanni**. Its R&D (CSO **Rafal Kaminski**, ex-UCB and Roche, since 2022) covers brain health — epilepsy (cenobamate), mood disorders (trazodone, lurasidone), neurodevelopmental disorders — plus pain/inflammation and pediatrics. The R&D chain runs from computational and medicinal chemistry and pharmacology to **chemical scale-up and analytical development** (Guido's area) and clinical. R&D spend was **€46M in 2025** — modest for its size. In 2026 it bought Catalyst Pharmaceuticals ($4.1B) to enter the US and rare disease.

financials.text: **Angelini Industries revenue 2025:** €1.7B (+4.6%); €2.2B under old consolidation method. **Angelini Industries EBITDA 2025:** €229M (−3.8%). **Angelini Industries net income 2025:** €127M (2024: €156M). **Angelini Pharma revenue 2025:** €1.26B (+3.3%), ~¾ of group. **Angelini Pharma R&D 2025:** €46M. **Catalyst acquisition:** $4.1B equity value, closed Jul 16, 2026. **Catalyst 2025 sales:** $589M (Firdapse $358M, Agamree $117M, Fycompa $113M). **Angelini Ventures:** €300M fund; ~€125M invested in 22 companies. Private, family-owned group; figures from Angelini Industries' July 1, 2026 release and deal coverage. Group: ~5,600 employees, 21 countries.

Please write me at **guido.furlotti@angelinipharma.com**.” Juliana confirmed email would follow. **Oct 21:** Jenny Park (Meteor) emailed him, cc Amos — **opened 3 times, 6 link clicks** (last open Oct 21 evening), **no reply yet**. Box moved to *Contacted* on Oct 28.

industry.title: Spatial omics moves into CNS and rare disease
industry.text: Spatial and single-cell methods are increasingly used on small, heterogeneous tissues — resected epileptic brain, muscle biopsies — where bulk methods blur the signal. That is Meteor's sweet spot.

industry.title: European mid-caps buying US rare-disease assets
industry.text: Angelini's Catalyst deal is its US beachhead. Integration year = new rare-disease biology questions and new budgets, but also busy teams.

talking_points: Thanks for opening our note — I know drug substance is far from tissue biology. Who in Angelini's **disease biology & pharmacology** or translational team would be the right person to see SLACS?
With Catalyst, Angelini now owns **Agamree (Duchenne)** and **Firdapse (LEMS)** — is there in-house work on muscle or neuromuscular-junction biology, or is that done with academic partners?
For epilepsy, does your team work with **resected human brain tissue** (e.g., focal lesions)? Isolating the exact abnormal region is what SLACS does.
Does Angelini outsource biomarker and omics work to CROs, or build it in-house in Rome?
From your side: are there **impurity or cell-based assay** questions in CMC where precise cell isolation would matter? (Only if he shows interest.)
You already work with Korean partners like SK Biopharmaceuticals and Cureverse — how did those collaborations start?

attention.title: Fit is low — aim for a referral.
attention.text: Guido is CMC/chemistry. Don't pitch him hard; ask for one name in disease biology / translational science. A warm internal intro is the win.

attention.title: Follow up on email now.
attention.text: He clicked links 6 times on Oct 21 and has not replied for a week. Send a short reply-to-thread from Amos with the referral question.

attention.title: Parallel door.
attention.text: Consider separate outreach to Angelini's R&D leadership (CSO Rafal Kaminski's org) and to **Angelini Ventures** (Asia expansion), rather than relying on Guido only.
